mind_map.central_node: A Bottle of Dew: The Dignity of Labor and Illusion of Magic
plot_summary_nodes: Rama Natha inherits vast agricultural fields but neglects them entirely.
Obsessed with a legendary magic potion that turns objects to gold, he spends all his wealth on tricksters.
Sage Mahipati visits and offers a formula: collect 5 litres of winter morning dew from self-planted banana leaves.
Rama Natha clears his fields, plants banana trees, and diligently collects dew over six long years.
His wife Madhumati harvests and sells the bananas, earning a large pile of real gold coins.
When the dew fails to turn copper into gold, Sage Mahipati reveals the true gold earned through six years of honest labor.
character_arc_nodes: Rama Natha: Lazy, gullible seeker of quick shortcuts -> Hardworking, self-reliant, dedicated farmer.
Madhumati: Anxious wife fearing poverty -> Pragmatic business manager accumulating genuine wealth.
Sage Mahipati: Wise mentor who uses experiential learning and clever strategy to teach the value of labor.
theme_and_moral_nodes: Primary Theme: Hard work and perseverance are the true generators of wealth.
Secondary Theme: Magical shortcuts are dangerous illusions that lead to financial ruin.
Moral Lesson: True prosperity comes from physical labor, discipline, and productive effort.
key_grammar_nodes: Homophones: Words with identical sounds but different spellings/meanings (dew/due, son/sun, ate/eight).
Simple Past Tense: Regular (-ed) and irregular verb forms used for past events (planted, tended, collected, gave, bought).
